name: De Sano & Persinger 1987: 4 Hz across the temporal lobes, 15 min
summary: About 15 min of a 4 Hz sine field across the temporal lobes while watching a small green light flashing at 4 Hz and following imagery instructions, after De Sano & Persinger 1987. The original field (about 1.5 mT at the skull) is out of this helmet's reach, so only the timing is reproduced. The paper reports a lower heart rate and more floating or rising imagery after 4 Hz.
notes: The paper used one electromagnet per side: a 25 cm soft-iron nail wound with 1050 turns of 20-gauge wire, on a retractable arm 'just rostral to the upper half of the ear', driven with sine current at 1 or 4 Hz (De Sano 1987 p.1 [968]). Three groups of eight received sham (a constant light), 1 Hz or 4 Hz, with the Hypnotic Induction Profile before and after (pp.1-2 [968-969]). This program plays the 4 Hz arm: a 4 Hz sine on 1-ms points through one coil per side, both on together. The sites FT9h and FT10h are this project's reading of the paper's landmark. The green light is not part of the helmet: use a separate green lamp or screen flashing at 4 Hz; it will not be phase-locked to the field. Field: the paper gives about 15 gauss (1.5 mT) at the skull surface, 2 gauss (200 uT) at the temporal cortex, 0.5 gauss at the hippocampus and 0.2 gauss at the frontal lobes (p.1 [968]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT it is 200 times below the paper's cortex value. This helmet's ceiling (about 8 uT at 20 mm, 200 uT at the scalp) is still 25 times below at the cortex and 7.5 times below at the skull, so only the timing is the paper's. Support (p.2 [969]): lower heart rate after 4 Hz (F2,18 = 3.73), more vestibular references after 4 Hz (F = 11.50), and a sex by field interaction for the change in suggestibility (F = 4.90: women rose after 1 Hz, men after 4 Hz). 'More imaginings' (F = 3.13) is below the .05 criterion of 3.55. One lab, and no independent group has tested it. The light and the instructions are strong suggestions in themselves. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Flashing light can trigger seizures in photosensitive people. Not for people with epilepsy; stop on fear or distress.
setting: Sitting comfortably in a dimly lit room, watching a small green light 2 m away and about 15 degrees above the horizontal that flashes at 4 Hz, and following five imagery instructions: walking through a forest, a light in a clearing, the light approaching, the light enclosing you, a presence in the light. The Hypnotic Induction Profile before and after.
schedule: One exposure per person in the original (between groups). For a self-test, compare active and sham sessions in Blind mode on separate days, with the outcome decided in advance.
source: De Sano & Persinger 1987, Geophysical variables and behavior: XXXIX. Alterations in imaginings and suggestibility during brief magnetic field exposures, Percept Mot Skills 64:968-970 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3601616/ ; Richards, Persinger & Koren 1993, Modification of activation and evaluation properties of narratives by weak complex magnetic field patterns that simulate limbic burst firing, Int J Neurosci 71:71-85 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8407157/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/

phases.name: 4 Hz across both temporal lobes, green light at 4 Hz
